chunk: Recruitment & Onboarding Policy (EN, 202501) # Recruitment & Onboarding Policy Version: 202501 Company: Global Service Firm Region: Global (EN)

The purpose of this Recruitment & Onboarding Policy is to establish a clear and consistent framework for attracting, selecting, and integrating new employees into Global Service Firm. This policy applies to all departments and positions across the organization, ensuring that our recruitment and onboarding processes align with our core values and business objectives.

1. Fairness: All recruitment and onboarding activities will be conducted without discrimination based on race, gender, age, religion, sexual orientation, disability, or any other protected characteristic. 2. Transparency: Clear communication regarding the recruitment process and expectations will be maintained with all stakeholders. 3. Inclusivity: We strive to create a diverse workforce that reflects the communities we serve, promoting an inclusive environment for all candidates. 4. Compliance: All recruitment practices will comply with local, regional, and international labor laws and regulations. 5. Candidate Experience: We aim to provide a positive and engaging experience for all candidates throughout the recruitment and onboarding processes.

HR Department: Oversee the recruitment and onboarding processes. Ensure compliance with legal and regulatory requirements. Provide training and support to hiring managers. Hiring Managers: Identify staffing needs and initiate job requisitions. Collaborate with HR to develop job descriptions and select candidates. Recruiters: Source and screen candidates. Facilitate interviews and manage communication with candidates. Executives: Approve highlevel recruitment decisions and ensure alignment with organizational goals. New Hires: Actively participate in the onboarding process and provide feedback to improve future experiences.
Hiring managers submit a job requisition form to HR, detailing the position's responsibilities, qualifications, and urgency.
HR reviews the requisition and obtains necessary approvals from executives before proceeding.
HR collaborates with hiring managers to create clear and comprehensive job descriptions that outline essential functions and qualifications.
Job openings are posted on the company website, job boards, and social media platforms to attract a diverse pool of candidates.
Recruiters actively source candidates through networking, referrals, and partnerships with educational institutions.
Candidates are screened based on their qualifications and experience, followed by interviews and assessments.

1. Interviews: Structured interviews will be conducted by hiring managers and HR to assess candidates’ skills and cultural fit. 2. Assessments: Relevant assessments may be administered to evaluate specific skills or competencies. 3. Case Studies: Candidates may be asked to solve case studies relevant to the position to demonstrate their problemsolving abilities. 4. Reference Checks: HR will conduct reference checks to validate candidates' qualifications and past performance. 5. Background Checks: Background checks will be performed in accordance with local laws to ensure candidate integrity.

Global Service Firm is committed to being an equal opportunity employer. We actively work to mitigate bias in our recruitment processes by employing standardized evaluation criteria and diverse interview panels.
Candidates will be informed of their application status within two weeks of submission.
Constructive feedback will be provided to candidates who reach the interview stage but are not selected.
Successful candidates will receive a formal offer letter outlining salary, benefits, and start date.
New hires will receive a welcome email with essential information and resources prior to their start date.
New hires will attend an orientation session covering company policies, culture, and administrative procedures.
A structured induction program will be implemented, including training sessions and introductions to key team members.
New hires will undergo a probation period of 90 days, during which their performance will be evaluated.
Each new hire will be assigned a buddy or mentor to guide them through their initial days and help them acclimate to the company culture.

Applicant Tracking System (ATS): Used for managing job postings, applications, and candidate communications. Human Resource Information System (HRIS): Maintains employee records and facilitates onboarding processes. ELearning Platforms: Provide access to training materials and compliance courses during onboarding.

1. Length: The standard probation period is 90 days. 2. Evaluations: Performance evaluations will be conducted at 30, 60, and 90 days to assess fit and performance. 3. Extensions: Probation periods may be extended for an additional 30 days if performance does not meet expectations. 4. Termination: Employment may be terminated during the probation period if performance is unsatisfactory.

Mandatory Compliance Training: New hires must complete compliance training within their first week. Security Training: Training on data protection and security protocols will be provided. Culture Workshops: Workshops will be held to familiarize new hires with company values and culture.
A review will be conducted at the end of the first 90 days to discuss performance, set goals, and address any concerns.
New hires must submit required documentation, including identification, tax forms, and signed offer letters, before their start date.
Recruitment and onboarding practices will be adapted to meet local labor laws and regulations in each region where Global Service Firm operates.

1. What should I do if I need to fill a position urgently? Contact HR immediately to expedite the requisition process. 2. How long does the onboarding process take? The onboarding process typically lasts 90 days, including the probation period. 3. Can I request changes to the job description? Yes, changes can be requested during the job requisition process. 4. What if I have concerns about a new hire during the probation period? Discuss concerns with HR and the hiring manager to determine the best course of action. 5. Is training mandatory during onboarding? Yes, compliance and security training are mandatory for all new hires. 6. How will I receive feedback during my onboarding? Regular checkins will be scheduled to provide feedback and address any questions. 7. What happens if I don't meet performance expectations during probation? A performance review will be conducted, and if necessary, an extension or termination may occur. 8. How can I ensure a diverse candidate pool? Utilize diverse job boards and networks to reach a broader audience. 9. What digital tools will I use during onboarding? You will use the ATS for application tracking and the HRIS for employee records. 10. Who should I contact if I have questions about the onboarding process? Reach out to your HR representative for any inquiries.  This Recruitment & Onboarding Policy is designed to foster a structured, fair, and inclusive approach to hiring and integrating new employees into Global Service Firm. By adhering to these guidelines, we aim to enhance our organizational culture and ensure the success of our new hires.
